record.original_question: Analyze the Lanczos algorithm under general models of inexact matrix-vector multiplication and/or the use of a preconditioner. Progress is made if these bounds generalize Paige's analysis and/or provide new, easier to understand, insight into the behavior of the algorithm.

evidence.quote: Analyze the Lanczos algorithm under general models of inexact matrix-vector multiplication and/or the use of a preconditioner. Progress is made if these bounds generalize Paige's analysis and/or provide new, easier to understand, insight into the behavior of the algorithm.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ be a symmetric matrix and let $b \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with $\|b\|_2 = 1$. The Lanczos algorithm produces, in exact arithmetic, an orthonormal basis $\{q_1,\dots,q_k\}$ of the Krylov subspace $\mathcal{K}_k(A,b) = \mathrm{span}\{b, Ab, \dots, A^{k-1}b\}$ together with a symmetric tridiagonal matrix $T_k = Q_k^T A Q_k$ via the three-term recurrence
\[
\beta_{j+1} q_{j+1} = A q_j - \alpha_j q_j - \beta_j q_{j-1}, \qquad \alpha_j = q_j^T A q_j,
\]
with $q_1 = b$ and $\beta_1 = 0$. Paige's classical analysis bounds, in finite precision arithmetic, the residuals
\[
A Q_k - Q_k T_k - \beta_{k+1} q_{k+1} e_k^T = F_k,
\]
the local orthogonality $|q_{j+1}^T q_j|$, and the deviation $|q_j^T A q_j - \alpha_j|$ in terms of unit roundoff $\varepsilon$ and $\|A\|$, and uses these to relate convergence of Ritz values to loss of orthogonality.

Consider now an inexact Lanczos process in which the matrix-vector product $Av$ is replaced by $Av + g(v)$, where $g:\mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$ is a perturbation modeling either inexact matrix-vector multiplication (e.g., $\|g(v)\|_2 \le \eta_j \|v\|_2$ for a sequence of tolerances $\eta_j$) or the application of a preconditioner $M \approx A^{-1}$ (so that the recurrence is run with $M A$ or with an inexact action of $M$).

Provide rigorous a-priori bounds, in this inexact and/or preconditioned setting, on:
(i) the columnwise residual $\|F_k\|$ of the perturbed three-term recurrence;
(ii) the local loss of orthogonality $|q_{j+1}^T q_j|$ and the local discrepancy $|q_j^T A q_j - \alpha_j|$;
(iii) the resulting effect on Ritz value convergence,
in terms of $\varepsilon$, $\|A\|$, the perturbation sizes $\eta_j$, and (when applicable) spectral properties of the preconditioner. The bounds should reduce to Paige's bounds when $g \equiv 0$ and no preconditioner is used, and/or should yield qualitatively new, more transparent insight into the behavior of the inexact/preconditioned Lanczos algorithm.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature confirms that Paige's analysis governs unpreconditioned finite-precision Lanczos, and that extending such bounds to preconditioned and inexact-matvec variants remains an active and largely open research direction. Recent works (e.g., 2025 results on finite precision block Lanczos) continue to address related cases without producing a unified Paige-style theory for general inexact/preconditioned Lanczos.

status_evidence.title: On finite precision block Lanczos computations
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work extends Paige-style finite precision analysis to block Lanczos, indicating the general inexact/preconditioned case is still being developed.
status_evidence.claim: Generalizing Paige's analysis to broader Lanczos variants is an ongoing research effort.

status_evidence.title: The Lanczos and conjugate gradient algorithms in finite precision arithmetic
status_evidence.snippet: Although preconditioning represents an unavoidable and fundamental part of practical computations, research has concentrated on analysis of basic unpreconditioned algorithms.
status_evidence.claim: A finite-precision analysis at Paige's level of rigor for preconditioned Lanczos is acknowledged as not yet available.
